title: Creamy Grits with Butter and Chives
summary: Old-fashioned grits simmered gently in half milk, half water, then finished with butter and snipped chives.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, plus a pat to serve
chives, snipped, plus a few whole stalks to serve

steps.title: Heat the liquid
steps.text: Combine the milk, 500 ml water, salt and pepper in the heavy saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Stay close, as milk can foam up and over the edge in seconds.

steps.title: Whisk in the grits
steps.text: Pour the grits in slowly while whisking constantly. Adding them gradually lets each particle get wet separately, so you avoid lumps.

steps.title: Cook low and covered
steps.text: Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 20-25 min, whisking every few minutes and scraping the bottom where milk can catch. They are done when thick, creamy and tender with no gritty centre; add 2 tbsp water at a time if they get too stiff.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the 30 g butter and the snipped chives. Ladle into bowls and top each with a pat of butter and a few long chive stalks.

tips: Instant or quick grits will not give the same texture; use old-fashioned grits and allow the full time.
Not scraping the bottom is the usual mistake and leads to scorched milk; whisk regularly and keep the heat low.
Grits thicken as they stand, so loosen with hot water just before serving.
Stir in grated cheese at the end if you like.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 4 days; they set firm. Reheat in a pan with a splash of milk or water, whisking, until smooth and piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
